RFC4303-1-1.note: Re-judged after the R3 split: the row is now only the Section 1 clause 'MUST be configurable via management interfaces' (the IKE negotiation clause is the gap row RFC4303-1-2). Forbidden behaviour: the management interface refusing, or silently altering, an integrity-only ESP configuration. Positive: TestIPsecESPRequiresIntegrity drives esp + null cipher + sha256 through parseOSPFConfig/validateConfig and t.Fatalf on any refusal. Negative (R1(b), inputs pushed toward a refusal): TestRFC4303IntegrityOnlyESPIsConfigurable, for every integrity algorithm in ipsecAuthKeyLen x {cipher leaf omitted, explicit null}, validates and installs and asserts proto 50 (not AH), cipher null with no key, and the configured integrity algorithm and key length, so a validator requiring a cipher for ESP or accepting integrity-only for one algorithm only goes red. The old negative (null cipher with no integrity refused) proved RFC4303-3.2-1 and was removed from this row. Revert records on validateESPConfidentiality for both units observed red (positive recorded by this judge). Only the OSPFv3 manual-SA surface offers integrity-only ESP; IKE's absence is RFC4303-1-2.

RFC4303-1-2.note: First judgement. The Section 1 clause 'Integrity-only ESP MUST be offered as a service selection option, e.g., it must be negotiable in SA management protocols' is unmet in Ze's IKEv2: the ESP encryption vocabulary (ike/ipsec/types.go encryptionNames, ParseEncryptionAlgo) has no null entry, so no configuration can propose ENCR_NULL, and resolveESPTransforms (engine/initiator.go) resolves only registered ciphers; TestRFC7296NegotiationRefusesNullIntegrityAndNullCipher shows the matcher refuses a peer's null proposal. Integrity-only ESP is offered only by manual OSPFv3 SA configuration (RFC4303-1-1). The {gap} annotation and the Support remaining text disclose it; the row quote is a verbatim span of Section 1, split from RFC4303-1-1 under R3 with a correction paragraph and an extraction unsourced-ids entry.

RFC4303-2-1.note: Re-judged (was weak: the IKE Child SA producer was untagged). Both producers Ze fills are now covered. OSPFv3 manual SAs: TestRFC4303ESPPacketOnTheWireCarriesProtocol50 (netns, IPv6 Next Header 50 captured on the wire), negative TestRFC4303IntegrityOnlyESPOnTheWireIsNotAH (null cipher + sha256, the AH-shaped input, still 50 on the wire), TestIPsecSAProtocolNumber; ipsecProtoNumber revert records observed red. IKE Child SA: TestRFC4301ChildSAIsInstalledAsESP (tag only, body unchanged, D-15) asserts Proto 50 on the inbound and the outbound SA createFirstChildSA installs; installChildSA is the one SAParams builder of the engine (callers: first Child SA and CREATE_CHILD_SA), revert record observed red. The IKE side is single-polarity by construction: protoESP is a constant and IKEv2 offers no input that selects another protocol, so the row's negative stays the OSPF one. The SAParams-to-kernel step (dataplane xfrmStateFromParams) is shared by both producers and proven on the wire by the OSPF probe; the VPP backend is asserted only at the SAParams boundary Ze owns.

RFC4303-2.1-1.note: Re-read 2026-09-29 after RFC3948-2.1-1 tag lines were added above six units of rfc4303_peer_spi_test.go; no assertion changed. Every producer of an SPI Ze sends is now proven, both polarities. Ze's own SPI (SAi2/SAr2/rekey inbound): TestGenerateESPSPISkipsTheReservedZero scripts three zero draws and pins the first non-zero, discriminated by the spi != 0 mutant. The peer's SPI Ze sends on (rfc4303_peer_spi_test.go): initiator SAr2, responder SAi2, rekey request, rekey response each refuse 0 (no establish, no Child SA, no ESP state) through the real encrypted exchange, and each positive pins the exact peer SPI 0x0a0b0c0d on the outbound state; the same edited message on both sides isolates the SPI. Initiator negative also catches removal of the createFirstChildSA refusal (it asserts initiatorFirstChildSA fails with no ESP state). Responder negative's outSPI^1 break is the silent-substitution defect the initiator had; deleting either redundant refusal alone leaves it green, removing both reddens it. OSPF: TestIPsecSPIZeroRefused refuses spi 0 and accepts 4294967295. Caveats, not gaps: TestGenerateESPSPI (100 random draws, P(0)~2^-32) cannot fail on its own, and TestIPsecSPIBoundary's 255/256 pair tests the IANA 1..255 reservation, a neighbouring rule; both are redundant with the discriminating tests above.

RFC4303-2.1-2.note: Re-judged (was weak: the negotiation branch, the IKE Child SA, had no test). Manual-configuration branch unchanged: OSPFv3 TestRFC4303InboundESPSAKeyedOnConfiguredDestination plus the netns pair TestRFC4303InboundESPMapsByConfiguredDestination / TestRFC4303InboundESPToUnconfiguredDestinationMapsToNoSA, buildIPsecSA revert records observed red. Negotiation branch: positive TestRFC4303InboundChildSAKeyedOnNegotiatedSPIAndLocalAddress (the single inbound SA carries the negotiated ChildInboundSPI, proto 50 and Dst = the negotiated local address, so a Src/Dst swap goes red); negative TestRFC4303InboundESPToAnotherLocalAddressMapsToNoSA on real XFRM in a rootless netns (control to negotiated 10.250.0.1: delivered, XfrmInNoStates +0; same SPI and packet to 10.250.0.3: not delivered, XfrmInNoStates +1). Judge re-ran it once under -race: body ran in the child namespace and passed; judge mutation (negative packet aimed at the negotiated address) went red on the not-delivered assertion, so the negative is not vacuous. installChildSA revert records observed red for both. The indication itself (destination matched, source not) is XFRM's (daddr, spi, proto) state lookup keyed on what Ze negotiated, so both branches are proven for every role Ze fills; VPP backend inbound lookup is asserted only at the SAParams boundary.

RFC4303-2.2.1-2.note: Forbidden behaviour: keying an SA with ESN that the SA management protocol did not negotiate. Negative: TestEsnInitiatorRefusesAnESNValueItNeverOffered requires verifyAcceptedOffer to return errAcceptedOfferESN for an answer selecting ESN (and for two ESN values), t.Fatalf otherwise. Positive: the offered non-ESN value is accepted and the offer is pinned to the single value. Ze never offers ESN and manual OSPFv3 SAs set none, so no un-negotiated ESN path exists.

RFC4303-3.2-1.note: Re-judged: TestIPsecESPRequiresIntegrity changed only by removing the RFC4303-1-1 negative comment; its assertions are unchanged. Forbidden behaviour: an ESP SA with both encryption and integrity NULL. Negative: validateConfig(esp, encryption-algorithm null, no integrity) must return ErrIPsecAuthAlgo, t.Fatalf otherwise. Positive: null cipher + sha256 accepted (exactly one service). The only producer that admits a NULL cipher is the OSPFv3 manual path; the IKE ESP vocabulary has no ENCR_NULL (ike/ipsec/types.go encryptionNames), so every IKE Child SA carries encryption. Both clauses are the same obligation and both are covered.

RFC4303-3.4.3-1.note: Forbidden behaviour: Ze unable to run a receive window of at least 32 on a 32-bit-sequence SA (e.g. installing a smaller window). TestChildSAReplayWindowDefault (engine/child_test.go) asserts ReplayWin == 64 on both installed SAs; a window below 32 fails it. Ze never negotiates ESN, so every SA uses 32-bit sequence numbers. Single-polarity marker present. The assertion is at SAParams; xfrmStateFromParams projects it to the kernel (xfrm_linux.go:132).

RFC4303-3.4.3-2.note: Re-judged. {single-polarity} rightly dropped: the OSPFv3 producer has a refusal path. Positive: TestRFC4303ESPReplayWindowCarriesIntegrity installs replay-window 64 with null and aes128 ciphers and asserts every SA has ReplayWin 64, AuthAlgo sha256 and a 32-octet key; IKE: TestChildSAReplayRequiresIntegrity asserts every installed Child SA with ReplayWin > 0 is AEAD or carries AuthAlgo+AuthKey (non-AEAD proposals always resolve an integrity transform, resolveESPTransforms). Negative: TestRFC4303ESPReplayWindowWithoutIntegrityIsRefused, replay-window 64 with no integrity under no cipher, null and aes128, each refused ErrIPsecAuthAlgo by validateConfig, so anti-replay without integrity never reaches the installer. The refusal comes from the integrity-always-required check, which is exactly how Ze meets this MUST NOT; the input enables anti-replay without integrity, so it violates this requirement. Records: buildIPsecSA (positive) and validateIPsecInterface (negative) reverts observed red. Supplementary gap: the IKE negative (a non-AEAD proposal with no INTEG never installed) is structural, not tested.

RFC4303-3.4.3-4.note: Forbidden behaviour (SHOULD): a default window other than 64. TestChildSAReplayWindowDefault asserts ReplayWin == 64 on both IKE Child SAs with no window configured; any other default goes red. Single-polarity marker present. The OSPFv3 manual path defaults to no anti-replay, which RFC 4303 Section 3.3.3 advises for manually keyed SAs, so the default-window sentence binds the IKE path.
